qa_pair.question: For the property sc-domain:seobandwagon.com over 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-07 (web search), what is the true page-impression count — i.e. total impressions counted per page rather than per property? Return the integer.

For sc-domain:seobandwagon.com over 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-07, what fraction of the property's true impression total do the query-dimension rows account for? Return the percentage rounded to the nearest whole number.

For sc-domain:seobandwagon.com over 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-07, which page contributes the largest share of the sitewide position mass (sum of position × impressions across pages), and what is that share as a percentage of the total position mass, rounded to the nearest whole number? Answer as "URL, N%".
Request the top 25 queries by impressions for sc-domain:seobandwagon.com over 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-07. Which query ranks #1, and how many impressions does it have? Answer as "query, N".

Across all sitemaps submitted for sc-domain:seobandwagon.com, how many sitemap FILE errors (problems reading the sitemap files themselves, as reported by the Sitemaps API) are there in total, and what is the URL of the sitemap with the oldest last-download date by Google? Answer as "N, URL".

For sc-domain:seobandwagon.com over 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-07, the property-level impression total and the sum of impressions across per-page rows are two different numbers. State both as "propertyTotal vs pageSum".
Inspect the URL https://seobandwagon.com/seo-services on the property sc-domain:seobandwagon.com. What are the index-status verdict and the coverageState? Answer as "VERDICT, coverageState".

For sc-domain:seobandwagon.com over 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-07, does the sum of daily impressions (grouping by date) exactly equal the impression total with no dimensions at all? Answer "yes N" or "no N vs M" using the number(s) you measured.
How many search-appearance (rich result) types are recorded for sc-domain:seobandwagon.com over 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-07? Return the integer count.

For sc-domain:seobandwagon.com over 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-07, the sitewide average position (byProperty) is about 45.6 while the page https://seobandwagon.com/seo-services averages position ~5.1. If that page lost all of its impressions, would the sitewide average position number get larger (worse) or smaller (better)? Answer "larger" or "smaller".
